rows.headline: StoneX fell 27% after quarterly profit came in well below what analysts expected
rows.summary: StoneX reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.66 per share against roughly $0.92 expected. Revenue grew 12% but net income slipped 2% as interest and pay costs rose faster than revenue.

rows.headline: SELLAS fell another 17% as it raises $150 million after its 156% jump on leukemia trial data
rows.summary: SELLAS shares more than doubled on November 17 when its cancer vaccine succeeded in a pivotal trial, and the company announced a $150 million share sale the same evening. The stock has been falling since as investors absorb the new shares.

rows.headline: Williams-Sonoma dropped 15% as adjusted profit fell just short and the full-year outlook was not raised
rows.summary: Comparable sales rose 5.1% and every brand grew, but adjusted EPS of $2.19 was slightly below the roughly $2.21 analysts expected, most of the margin improvement came from one-off tariff refunds, and the company only reiterated its full-year guidance.

rows.headline: NetEase fell 11% after revenue declined and earnings missed estimates
rows.summary: NetEase reported a 1.8% fall in third-quarter revenue, with its core games business down 1.7%, and earnings per share about 12% below what analysts expected. For a company valued on steady growth in games, a quarter of shrinking sales was enough for a double-digit drop.

rows.headline: PDD Holdings rose 11% as profit beat expectations even though revenue did not grow
rows.summary: PDD’s third-quarter revenue was flat at RMB108.3 billion, but earnings came in about 12% above analyst estimates because the Temu owner cut sales and marketing spending by RMB5 billion. Investors had feared profit would fall.

rows.headline: Valvoline gained 10% after same-store sales rose 9.4% and it guided to another year of growth
rows.summary: Valvoline’s fiscal fourth-quarter sales grew 22% with same-store sales up 9.4%, its 20th straight year of same-store growth, and it forecast fiscal 2027 same-store growth of 5% to 7% with up to 220 new stores.
